newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close up on strong technical rebound.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close up on strong technical rebound.

text.p: South Korean stocks rallied strongly in a technical rebound on Tuesday following the previous day's sell-off, traders said.
But with no fundamental positive news to sustain the rally, traders said they expected prices to decline again from Thursday or Friday. All markets will be closed on Wednesday for Buddha's Birthday.
The Korea composite price index closed at 683.86 points on Tuesday, up 11.76 points or 1.75 percent. Gainers outnumbered decliners by 604 to 201. Trading volume was 35.91 million shares.
Trading volume for Daewoo Heavy was 2.51 million shares.
Export-related shares, which stand to gain from the yen's strength against the dollar, also rebounded strongly.
LG Electronics shares rose 4.95 percent or 500 won to 10,600, while Yukong jumped 6.21 percent or 900 won to 15,400.
Hyundai Motor rose 500 won or 2.24 percent to 22,800 and Korean Air Line was up 6.72 percent or 900 won to 14,300.
Hanwha Merchant Bank rose by its daily limit to 16,400 won on expectations that a favourable court ruling would lead to an internal takeover battle.

The ruling, reportedly issued on Tuesday, was in a dispute between majority shareholder Hanwha Group and the second largest shareholder, Park Eui-song. Hanwha disputed Park's claim the ruling favoured him. Independent confirmation was unavailable.
"If it's true that today's ruling favours Park, this will spark another battle for control of the bank which will boost share prices," said Kim Byong-seok, Hannuri-Salomon Securities analyst.
Shares of Midopa Department Store and Dainong Corp, flagship of Midopa's parent Dainong Group, went limit low to 9,400 and 3,220 won respectively.
Both shares have been battered by rumours of liquidity problems at Midopa. The retailer has denied the rumours.

S.W. Choi, chief trade at Schroders Securities, said Dainong's market influence may be over. "People are beginning to think it's just something that involves Dainong and it is not relevant to other companies," he said.
Traders said investors would be watching over the holiday for new developments in the scandal involving President Kim Young-sam's son.
